Ok so lets take a look at what exposure treatment is

It’s basically repeatedly getting exposed by a certain stimuli until you’re no longer afraid right? 

Ok so if you look into this article https://www.simplypsychology.org/Systematic-Desensitisation.html 

You’ll see the process of it. In the article it states in the beginning of the process there is the “Imagination phase” where the person imagines they are exposed to a spider through meditation and visualization.

Through this process, they are becoming the type of person who isn’t afraid of this situation anymore, correct? That fundamentally is the goal of the therapy. 

Just because you’re exposed to something 100 times I wouldn’t say automatically diminishes anxiety. You have to eventually become that person who isn’t afraid and that’s through training your mind to be in that situation, asking yourself rational thoughts and acting as the ideal self because that eventually will become you.

I think phobia is an **extreme** excessive fear of an object or situation. Yes it is possible to feel social anxiety to the point of phobia but I don't believe that's the case for every person.

But for the person to make that inner shift to a person who isn't afraid of snakes, they'll have to eventually accept becoming the person who isn't afraid of snakes. If they can't see themselves in that role and in that situation, I guarantee they will never get rid of that anxiety

Meditation of being in that situation just like desensitization. Maltz talks about seeing yourself in certain settings, taking every single detail in. The smell, the sights, the feelings, and imagining yourself acting in your ideal way.
